title: Strong feelings and how things look
summary: Expressing feelings you can't control ({てしょうがない}, {てたまらない}, {てならない}, {ずにはいられない}), exclamations ({ことか}), strong impressions ({ものがある}), and how someone appears ({げ}, {気味[ぎみ]}).

points.title: 〜てしょうがない / 〜て仕方[しかた]がない
points.meaning: so ... I can't stand it; extremely
points.structure: V-て / い-adj くて / な-adj で + しょうがない（仕方[しかた]がない・仕方[しかた]ない）
points.explanation:
Literally "there is no way (to deal with it)", this pattern says a feeling or sensation is so strong the speaker can't control it. It is the **most casual and most flexible** of the three "unbearably" patterns in this unit.

It works with emotions ({うれしくて}), physical sensations ({痛[いた]くて}), desires ({〜たくて}) and also with things that just keep bothering you ({気[き]になってしょうがない}, {眠[ねむ]くてしょうがない}).

{しょうがない} is the spoken form of {仕方[しかた]がない}. Normally it describes the speaker's own feelings; for other people add {〜ようだ} or {〜らしい}.

examples.jp: 試験[しけん]の結果[けっか]が気[き]になってしょうがない。
examples.en: I can't stop worrying about my exam results.

examples.jp: 昨日[きのう]から歯[は]が痛[いた]くてしょうがない。
examples.en: My tooth has been killing me since yesterday.

examples.jp: 来週[らいしゅう]の旅行[りょこう]が楽[たの]しみでしょうがない。
examples.en: I'm so excited about next week's trip I can hardly stand it.

examples.jp: うちの子犬[こいぬ]がかわいくて仕方[しかた]がない。
examples.en: Our puppy is just unbearably cute.

points.notes: Don't confuse with {〜てもしょうがない} ("there's no point in..."): {今[いま]さら悔[く]やんでもしょうがない} = "there's no use regretting it now".

quiz.q: 冷房[れいぼう]が壊[こわ]れて、暑[あつ]く＿＿。
quiz.en: The air conditioner broke and it's unbearably hot.

quiz.q: 何度[なんど]も同[おな]じミスをする自分[じぶん]が情[なさ]けなく＿＿。
quiz.en: I feel so pathetic for making the same mistake again and again.
choices: ても仕方[しかた]がない

points.title: 〜てたまらない
points.structure: V-て / い-adj くて / な-adj で + たまらない
points.explanation:
{たまらない} comes from {堪[たま]る} ("to endure"), so the pattern means "so ... that I can't endure it". It expresses an intense, often physical or emotional state: loneliness, joy, thirst, itchiness, a desire to see someone.

Compared with {てしょうがない}, it focuses more strongly on the **intensity of a feeling or bodily sensation**, and is slightly less casual. It is less natural with neutral states like {気[き]になる}.

It is very common with {〜たくてたまらない} ("dying to...").

examples.jp: 喉[のど]が渇[かわ]いてたまらない。
examples.en: I'm desperately thirsty.

examples.jp: 合格[ごうかく]の知[し]らせを聞[き]いて、うれしくてたまらなかった。
examples.en: When I heard I'd passed, I was overjoyed.

examples.jp: 一人暮[ひとりぐ]らしを始[はじ]めたばかりの頃[ころ]は、寂[さび]しくてたまらなかった。
examples.en: When I'd just started living alone, I was unbearably lonely.

examples.jp: 早[はや]く国[くに]の家族[かぞく]に会[あ]いたくてたまらない。
examples.en: I'm dying to see my family back home.

points.notes: {たまらない} on its own can also mean "irresistible": {この香[かお]り、たまらない！} ("This smell is amazing!").

quiz.q: 一日中[いちにちじゅう]何[なに]も食[た]べていないので、おなかがすいて＿＿。
quiz.en: I haven't eaten anything all day, so I'm starving.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]に会[あ]い＿＿たまらない。

points.title: 〜てならない
points.structure: V-て / い-adj くて / な-adj で + ならない
points.explanation:
{てならない} describes a feeling that **wells up by itself** and won't go away. It is more formal and written than the other two patterns, and it is used mainly with:
- verbs of spontaneous perception: {気[き]がしてならない}, {思[おも]えてならない}, {感[かん]じられてならない}
- emotional adjectives: {心配[しんぱい]でならない}, {残念[ざんねん]でならない}, {不安[ふあん]でならない}

It is **not** normally used for physical sensations such as hunger or heat; use {てたまらない} or {てしょうがない} for those.

Summary of the three:
- {しょうがない}: casual, widest range
- {たまらない}: intense emotions and bodily sensations
- {ならない}: written, spontaneous feelings and impressions

examples.jp: 将来[しょうらい]のことが心配[しんぱい]でならない。
examples.en: I'm terribly worried about the future.

examples.jp: 何[なに]か大切[たいせつ]なことを忘[わす]れているような気[き]がしてならない。
examples.en: I can't shake the feeling that I've forgotten something important.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]が嘘[うそ]をついているように思[おも]えてならない。
examples.en: I can't help thinking that he's lying.

examples.jp: 恩師[おんし]が亡[な]くなったと聞[き]き、残念[ざんねん]でならない。
examples.en: I heard that my old teacher has passed away, and I am deeply saddened.

points.notes: Different from {〜てはならない} ("must not"): {嘘[うそ]をついてはならない} = "you must not lie".

quiz.q: あの日[ひ]、もっと早[はや]く連絡[れんらく]していれば助[たす]けられたような気[き]がして＿＿。
quiz.en: I can't shake the feeling that I could have helped if I'd contacted them sooner that day.

quiz.q: 事故[じこ]で亡[な]くなった方々[かたがた]のことを思[おも]うと、残念[ざんねん]＿＿。
quiz.en: When I think of the people who died in the accident, I feel deep regret.

points.title: 〜ずにはいられない
points.meaning: can't help doing; can't stop oneself from
points.structure: V-ない stem + ずにはいられない（する → せずにはいられない）
points.explanation:
{ず} is the classical form of {ない}, so this means "can't stay without doing": the speaker is compelled to act or react, often against their will. Common verbs: {笑[わら]う}, {泣[な]く}, {言[い]う}, {考[かんが]える}, {感[かん]じる}.

The spoken variant {〜ないではいられない} has the same meaning. Both are mainly used for the speaker's own reactions.

Irregular form: {する} becomes {せず}: {感動[かんどう]せずにはいられない}.

examples.jp: その映画[えいが]のラストシーンでは、泣[な]かずにはいられなかった。
examples.en: I couldn't help crying at the final scene of that film.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の話[はなし]があまりにおかしくて、笑[わら]わずにはいられなかった。
examples.en: His story was so funny I couldn't stop myself from laughing.

examples.jp: 困[こま]っている人[ひと]を見[み]ると、声[こえ]をかけずにはいられない。
examples.en: When I see someone in trouble, I can't help speaking to them.

examples.jp: 新[あたら]しいゲームが出[で]ると、買[か]わないではいられない。
examples.en: Whenever a new game comes out, I just have to buy it.

examples.jp: この記事[きじ]を読[よ]むと、政府[せいふ]の対応[たいおう]に疑問[ぎもん]を感[かん]じずにはいられない。
examples.en: Reading this article, one can't help questioning the government's response.

points.notes: Don't confuse with {〜ずにすむ} ("get away without doing") or {〜ざるを得[え]ない} ("have no choice but to", an outside obligation rather than an inner impulse).

quiz.q: あまりに理不尽[りふじん]な話[はなし]で、抗議[こうぎ]せ＿＿。
quiz.en: It was so unreasonable that I couldn't help protesting.
choices: ずにはいられなかった

quiz.q: 人[ひと]が困[こま]っているのを見[み]ると、助[たす]け＿＿いられない。
quiz.en: When I see someone in trouble, I can't help but help them.

points.title: 〜ことか
points.structure: どんなに / どれほど / 何度[なんど] ... + Plain form + ことか　（な-adj: な / である）
points.explanation:
{ことか} turns a statement into an emotional exclamation about degree: "how happy I was!", "how long I waited!". It usually pairs with a question word of degree: {どんなに}, {どれほど}, {どれだけ}, {何度[なんど]}, {何回[なんかい]}.

It sounds heartfelt and a little literary, so you will find it in letters, speeches, essays and dramatic dialogue. In casual talk people would more often say {すごく〜た}.

Don't confuse it with {ものか}, which is a strong denial ("as if I would!").

examples.jp: 合格[ごうかく]の知[し]らせを聞[き]いて、どんなにうれしかったことか。
examples.en: How happy I was to hear I'd passed!

examples.jp: 君[きみ]からの連絡[れんらく]を、どれほど待[ま]っていたことか。
examples.en: You have no idea how long I waited to hear from you.

examples.jp: この仕事[しごと]を辞[や]めたいと思[おも]ったことが、何度[なんど]あったことか。
examples.en: I can't count how many times I've wanted to quit this job.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]に来[き]たばかりの頃[ころ]、同僚[どうりょう]の親切[しんせつ]にどれだけ助[たす]けられたことか。
examples.en: When I'd just arrived in Japan, my colleagues' kindness helped me more than I can say.

quiz.q: 一人[ひとり]で外国[がいこく]に住[す]み始[はじ]めた頃[ころ]は、どんなに心細[こころぼそ]かった＿＿。
quiz.en: When I first started living abroad alone, how lonely and uneasy I felt!

quiz.q: あなたが無事[ぶじ]だと聞[き]いて、＿＿安心[あんしん]したことか。
quiz.en: You can't imagine how relieved I was to hear you were safe.

points.title: 〜ものがある
points.meaning: there is something (moving / impressive / hard) about it
points.structure: Plain form (V / い-adj / な-adj な) + ものがある
points.explanation:
{ものがある} expresses the speaker's strong impression that something has a certain quality, without pointing to one exact feature: "there's something touching about it", "it is pretty tough".

It often combines with verbs of emotion or evaluation: {心[こころ]を打[う]つものがある}, {胸[むね]に迫[せま]るものがある}, {光[ひか]るものがある} (shows promise), {驚[おどろ]くべきものがある}, or with adjectives like {つらい}, {厳[きび]しい}.

It is used in reviews, commentary and thoughtful conversation. It sounds measured and adult.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の演奏[えんそう]には、人[ひと]の心[こころ]を動[うご]かすものがある。
examples.en: There's something about his playing that moves people.

examples.jp: 毎日[まいにち]満員電車[まんいんでんしゃ]で通勤[つうきん]するのは、つらいものがある。
examples.en: Commuting on a packed train every day is pretty rough.

examples.jp: この町[まち]の変化[へんか]の速[はや]さには、驚[おどろ]くべきものがある。
examples.en: The speed at which this town is changing is quite astonishing.

examples.jp: 新人[しんじん]ながら、彼女[かのじょ]の企画力[きかくりょく]には光[ひか]るものがある。
examples.en: Although she's new, her planning skills really stand out.

quiz.q: この写真[しゃしん]には、見[み]る人[ひと]の胸[むね]に迫[せま]る＿＿がある。
quiz.en: There's something about this photo that deeply moves the viewer.

quiz.q: 四十代[よんじゅうだい]で一[いち]から転職[てんしょく]するのは、正直[しょうじき]厳[きび]しい＿＿。
quiz.en: Honestly, changing careers from scratch in your forties is pretty tough.

points.title: 〜げ
points.structure: い-adj stem / な-adj stem / V-たい stem + げ（な / に / だ）
points.explanation:
{げ} describes how a feeling or state **shows on the outside**: {悲[かな]しげな顔[かお]} (a sad-looking face), {楽[たの]しげに笑[わら]う} (laugh happily). It behaves like a {な}-adjective.

It is mostly literary or written and is used for other people's visible emotions. Common words: {寂[さび]しげ}, {楽[たの]しげ}, {不安[ふあん]げ}, {得意[とくい]げ}, {意味[いみ]ありげ} (meaningful-looking), {言[い]いたげ} (looking as if wanting to say something).

In modern slang {よさげ} ("looks good") is common online.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもたちが公園[こうえん]で楽[たの]しげに遊[あそ]んでいる。
examples.en: The children are playing happily in the park.

examples.jp: 少女[しょうじょ]は寂[さび]しげな目[め]で窓[まど]の外[そと]を見[み]ていた。
examples.en: The girl was gazing out the window with lonely eyes.

examples.jp: 面接[めんせつ]を待[ま]つ学生[がくせい]たちは、みんな不安[ふあん]げだった。
examples.en: The students waiting for their interviews all looked anxious.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は何[なに]か言[い]いたげな顔[かお]をしていたが、結局[けっきょく]何[なに]も言[い]わなかった。
examples.en: He looked as if he wanted to say something, but in the end he said nothing.

points.notes: {そう} is the everyday equivalent and also predicts events ({雨[あめ]が降[ふ]りそう}). {げ} cannot predict events: ✗ {雨[あめ]が降[ふ]りげ}.

quiz.q: 母[はは]は駅[えき]で、寂[さび]し＿＿に手[て]を振[ふ]っていた。
quiz.en: At the station, my mother waved with a lonely look.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]は何[なに]か言[い]いた＿＿な様子[ようす]だった。
quiz.en: She looked as though she wanted to say something.

points.title: 〜気味[ぎみ]
points.meaning: a touch of; slightly; tending toward (something negative)
points.structure: V-ます stem / Noun + 気味[ぎみ]（だ / の）
points.explanation:
{気味[ぎみ]} says that a person or thing is **slightly** in some (usually undesirable) state right now: a touch of a cold, a bit tired, running a little behind. It softens the statement, which makes it very useful at work: {少[すこ]し遅[おく]れ気味[ぎみ]です} sounds less alarming than {遅[おく]れています}.

Common combinations: {風邪[かぜ]気味[ぎみ]}, {疲[つか]れ気味[ぎみ]}, {太[ふと]り気味[ぎみ]}, {遅[おく]れ気味[ぎみ]}, {緊張[きんちょう]気味[ぎみ]}, {不足[ふそく]気味[ぎみ]}.

It works as a noun: {気味[ぎみ]だ}, {気味[ぎみ]の}, {気味[ぎみ]で}.

examples.jp: 今日[きょう]は少[すこ]し風邪[かぜ]気味[ぎみ]なので、早[はや]めに帰[かえ]ります。
examples.en: I've got a touch of a cold today, so I'll head home early.

examples.jp: 最近[さいきん]、仕事[しごと]が忙[いそが]しくて疲[つか]れ気味[ぎみ]だ。
examples.en: Work has been busy lately and I'm a bit worn out.

examples.jp: 初[はじ]めてのプレゼンで、彼[かれ]は少[すこ]し緊張[きんちょう]気味[ぎみ]だった。
examples.en: It was his first presentation, and he seemed a little nervous.

examples.jp: 工事[こうじ]の進[すす]み具合[ぐあい]がやや遅[おく]れ気味[ぎみ]です。
examples.en: Construction is running slightly behind schedule.

points.notes: {気味[ぎみ]} = a slight degree of a state now ({風邪[かぜ]気味[ぎみ]}). {がち} = something tends to happen often ({休[やす]みがち}, often absent). {っぽい} = has the feel of ({子[こ]どもっぽい}).

quiz.q: 寝不足[ねぶそく]が続[つづ]いて、ちょっと疲[つか]れ＿＿だ。
quiz.en: I haven't been sleeping enough, so I'm a bit tired.

quiz.q: 作業[さぎょう]が予定[よてい]より遅[おく]れ＿＿なので、来週[らいしゅう]から人[ひと]を増[ふ]やします。
quiz.en: The work is running a little behind schedule, so we'll add more people from next week.
